reels.title: Nvidia (NVDA): bull vs. bear

scenes.headline: Should Nvidia be on your watchlist?
scenes.body: It moved -5.7% today, one of the biggest moves among large caps. Here's the bull case, the bear case and the numbers. You decide.

scenes.headline: What the company does
scenes.body:
NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments.

Sector: **Technology**

scenes.headline: 🐂 The bull case
items: Fast growth: revenue up **106%** from a year ago
Very profitable: keeps **64¢** of profit from every $1 of sales
Generates $41.8B of free cash flow a year
56 Wall Street analysts cover it, with a consensus of **strong buy**

scenes.headline: 🐻 The bear case
items: Down 27% in three months, so the market has doubts
Volatile: historically moves about 2.2× as much as the market
Tech moves fast: competitors, new platforms or a slowdown in corporate IT spending can erode growth

scenes.headline: What to watch next
scenes.body: Next earnings report expected around **Tue, Nov 17**. Watch revenue growth, margins and especially guidance, since that's what moves the stock.

scenes.question: NVDA trades at $164.73 and analysts expect $15.91 of earnings per share next year. What's its forward P/E?
scenes.explain: $164.73 ÷ $15.91 ≈ 10.4. Investors pay about $10 for each $1 of expected profit.
